tex_content.html:
Lemma
[Weighted Schauder estimate] 1. ch6:6.20\group gt-ch06 If $u\in C^{2,\alpha }(\Omega )$ solves $Lu=f$, (6.12)--(6.13) hold, and $|u|_{0;\Omega }^{(-\beta )}$, $|f|_{0,\alpha ;\Omega }^{(2-\beta )}$ are finite, then \begin{equation} \tag {6.50} |u|_{2,\alpha ;\Omega }^{(-\beta )} \le C\bigl(|u|_{0;\Omega }^{(-\beta )}+|f|_{0,\alpha ;\Omega }^{(2-\beta )}\bigr), \end{equation} where $C=C(n,\alpha ,\lambda ,\Lambda ,\beta )$.
Proof

\sketch Apply Theorem 6.2 on $B_{d_x/2}(x)$ and multiply by the appropriate powers of $d_x$. This first gives

\begin{equation} \tag {6.51} |u|_{2;\Omega }^{(-\beta )} \leq C\bigl(|u|_{0;\Omega }^{(-\beta )} +|f|_{0,\alpha ;\Omega }^{(2-\beta )}\bigr). \end{equation}

For the Hölder term split into $|x-y|\le d_x/4$ and its complement, then take the supremum.

□
